indicatorNotes.creating: the letters of the fodder are used to make something new

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Someone builds an electronic circuit and calls it art.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like furniture but is someone who draws; a caricaturist draws exaggerated portraits.
annotation.definitionFit: A caricaturist is an artist who draws comic exaggerated likenesses.

indicatorNotes.missing header: the word loses its head, its first letter

blocks.note: a scoop is a story one paper has before the rest
SCOOP without its first letter S

annotation.surface: A newspaper's big exclusive runs without its headline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' wants to be the writing tool that fits the newspaper picture; here it is an enclosure for animals.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a poultry enclosure is a pen, just as a sheep pen is.

entries.clue: Company put chopped acorn outside for animal (7)

indicatorNotes.chopped: the acorn is cut up, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.outside: the rearranged letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: ACORN rearranged
CO is the usual abbreviation for company

annotation.surface: Someone chops up an acorn to feed a wild creature.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Company' sits at the start of the clue as if it were the subject, but it is the piece that ends up in the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the masked, ringtailed North American mammal is an animal.

blocks.note: the finest part of anything, as in the pick of the crop
the fatty part of milk

annotation.surface: A question about which dairy product is the finest.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the two senses are run together as if one were describing the other.
annotation.definitionFit: Cream is both the elite of a group and the rich part of milk.

entries.clue: One with a key job in the office? (6)

annotation.definition: One with a key job in the office?

blocks.note: reads as someone in a vital role; the setter means someone whose work is pressing keys
the workplace where that keyboard work is done; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: Someone who holds an important post at work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key job' reads as an important role, but it means a job done on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A typist works in an office pressing typewriter or keyboard keys all day.

blocks.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
allies are friends on your side

annotation.surface: Getting better with the right friends around you.
annotation.definitionFit: A patient or a market rallies when it recovers or improves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Right' is an adjective in the surface but just the letter R here.

entries.clue: Model at home makes a protest (3-2)

blocks.note: to sit is to pose for an artist, as a model does
in = at home

annotation.surface: A model staying at home stages a protest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Model' is a verb here: to sit for a portrait.
annotation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave.

indicatorNotes.not initially: the word goes without its first letter

blocks.note: TEN without its first letter T
a gross is twelve dozen, 144

annotation.surface: A puzzling list of numbers to take in.
annotation.walkthrough: A gross is an old counting unit worth knowing: twelve dozen, 144.
annotation.definitionFit: To engross is to absorb someone's attention completely.

entries.clue: Where to put chalk at the right moment (2,3)

blocks.note: snooker and pool players chalk the tip of the cue
exactly when prompted, as an actor's entrance is

annotation.surface: Advice on when and where to chalk up during a game of pool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chalk' suggests a blackboard, but it is the chalk a snooker player rubs on the tip of the cue.
annotation.definitionFit: On cue means exactly at the expected time.

entries.clue: Throw ring in, beside pack of cyclists (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the ring goes inside the throw

blocks.note: to pelt is to throw things at
O is ring-shaped
on = beside, as a town on a river

annotation.surface: Someone tosses a ring in next to a bunch of racing cyclists.
annotation.walkthrough: PEL(O)T followed by ON.
annotation.definitionFit: The peloton is the main group of riders in a road race.

entries.clue: Police chief to pay for some hesitation (12)

blocks.note: to commission a work is to order and pay for it
er is the sound of hesitating

annotation.surface: A top police officer paying for a moment's pause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Some hesitation' is not an extraction; ER is simply one hesitant noise.
annotation.definitionFit: A commissioner heads a police force, as in the Metropolitan Police.

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
I is the Roman numeral one
some = a bit, a certain amount

annotation.surface: Being top of the list is slightly disagreeable.
annotation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or unpleasant, especially of a smell.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number one' looks like a single phrase meaning the best, but it splits into two abbreviations.

blocks.note: ounce is another name for the snow leopard
an ounce is a small unit of weight, about 28 grams

annotation.surface: Some very light snow leopards.
annotation.walkthrough: The ounce as a big cat is an old name the solver may not know.
annotation.definitionFit: Ounces are both snow leopards and small units of weight.

entries.clue: Laid item to turn quickly into drink (3-4)

blocks.note: an egg is what a hen lays
to flip is to turn over fast

annotation.surface: Something laid is flipped over and made into a drink.
annotation.walkthrough: An egg-flip is a drink of beaten egg mixed with beer, wine or spirits, much like eggnog.
annotation.definitionFit: Egg-flip is a hot or cold drink made with beaten egg.

entries.clue: Hymns in addition to charity donations (6)

blocks.note: PS, postscript, is something added to a letter
alms are gifts to the poor

annotation.surface: A church service with hymns and a collection for charity.
annotation.definitionFit: Psalms are sacred songs, hymns from the Book of Psalms.
annotation.walkthrough: PS stands for postscript, the line added at the end of a letter.

indicatorNotes.first: tells you the fibbing piece comes before the other

blocks.note: fibbed = told a lie
to own is to have

annotation.surface: Someone told a fib and now wants a break.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' tells you the fibbing comes before the having, the reverse of the clue's order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rest by stretching out on a bed or sofa.

blocks.note: to make different
the coins jingling in your pocket

annotation.surface: Adjusting a handful of small coins.
annotation.definitionFit: The verb is a plain synonym for alter; the noun is the everyday word for coins of low value.
annotation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun share a spelling; 'small coins' is the money you get back after paying.

entries.clue: She rammed leg badly with heavy tool (12)

indicatorNotes.badly: the letters are put together badly, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A woman bashes her leg clumsily with a heavy tool.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is fitting: a sledgehammer is just what you would ram into a leg.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the big two-handed hammer used for breaking stone is a heavy tool.

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
Il Duce was the title of Mussolini; duce is Italian for leader

annotation.surface: Getting something out of a leader from eastern Italy.
annotation.walkthrough: Il Duce, 'the leader', was the title Mussolini took.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to draw out a response or fact from someone.

indicatorNotes.endless: the word loses its end, its last letter

blocks.note: misery = great sorrow
MISERY without its last letter Y

annotation.surface: The stingy person's unending unhappiness.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive but stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A miser is a skinflint who hoards money.

entries.clue: Parent ultimately to regret being faithful (4)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take what comes at the end, the last letter

blocks.note: the last letter of parent
to rue is to regret

annotation.surface: A parent who comes to regret staying loyal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a true friend is a loyal, faithful one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' points only at the word beside it, taking just its final letter.

blocks.note: Maud is a girl's name
L is the abbreviation for left
in = at home

annotation.surface: A tearful girl has left home.
annotation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully sentimental.
annotation.walkthrough: Maud is an old-fashioned girl's name, a familiar crossword staple.

indicatorNotes.in: the letter for caught goes inside the other word

blocks.note: sour = bitter-tasting
c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

annotation.surface: Someone is caught up in a resentful hunt.
annotation.walkthrough: C for caught comes from cricket scoring, where 'c' marks a catch.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to scour the countryside is to search every corner of it.

entries.clue: Another coming to cultivate fruit on bent cane (12)

indicatorNotes.bent: the cane is bent out of shape, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: to reap is to gather a crop you have grown
a pear is a fruit
CANE rearranged

annotation.surface: A gardener trains fruit along a bent cane for another crop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' just places PEAR before the rearranged CANE.
annotation.definitionFit: A reappearance is a second coming, arriving again.
